sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: AWS interview questions are unavoidable in any cloud-leaning backend interview — the core compute services (EC2 vs ECS vs EKS vs Fargate vs Lambda), RDS and Aurora and DynamoDB, S3 and storage classes, IAM (roles vs users, least privilege, the trust policy that always confuses), the messaging stack (SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge vs Kinesis), serverless patterns with Lambda + Spring Cloud Function, and the production-debug scenarios interviewers actually ask ("the AWS bill doubled overnight — debug it"). For vendor-agnostic cloud-native patterns (12-factor, deployment strategies, DR) see the Cloud Native page; for GCP and Azure see the dedicated platform pages.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Pick the **smallest** AWS service that does the job.

- **Compute** — Lambda < ECS Fargate < ECS / EKS < EC2.
- **Datastore** — DynamoDB for KV, RDS for relational, S3 for blobs.
- **Messaging** — SQS for queues, SNS for fan-out, EventBridge for rules, Kinesis for streams.
- **Identity** — IAM roles for everything; never long-lived keys.
- **Networking** — VPC, subnets, security groups, NACLs.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Aws core services** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Aws messaging** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Ecs and fargate** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Iam and security** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Rds with spring** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **S3 storage** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Serverless** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **IAM least-privilege** — explicit deny > implicit; trust policies trip people up.
- **S3 consistency** — strong read-after-write since 2020; pre-2020 trivia is outdated.
- **DynamoDB partition key** is permanent; pick to avoid hot partitions.
- **Lambda cold starts** — provisioned concurrency or SnapStart for Java.
- **Cost** — most expensive thing you forgot to turn off.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd run the service on <Lambda for spiky / Fargate for steady> behind <ALB | API Gateway>, store data in <DynamoDB | RDS> picked for <access pattern>, use SQS for buffering, attach IAM roles per-service, and put cost guardrails on day one."*
